Risk, controls and audit · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Mitigation plan tracking

Bruna · Risk and Controls Analyst

The risk team at a pharmaceutical company tracks 73 open mitigation plans, coming from the risk committee, health surveillance inspections and quality audits, spread across 26 owners.

When it runs
On the 1st and 15th of every month, reading the plans spreadsheet and the evidence folder, 5 business days before the monthly follow-up meeting; and with each owner email that reaches the risk team's inbox with the plan identifier in the subject
What it delivers in production
Each mitigation plan classified by evidence rather than by declaration, with the list of evidence requests and reschedulings to approve, delivered to the analyst twice a month before the follow-up meeting.
Who decides
Classifies and chases under analyst approval
Effort
Calibrate on 31 declared plans; two biweekly cycles
Set up5 steps · 10 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • what the Human AI reads
    empty
  • where it writes the result
    empty

Import Bruna with the JSON Importer

- The whole job is ONE SINGLE task and ends IN THIS SAME WAKE. If asked for a plan, propose EXACTLY ONE task, \"Process Input and write the PHARMAMITIGATE file to Output\", with every step inside it. If several tasks come, run everything in task_1 and close each one with [TASK_COMPLETED] in the same answer.

IDENTITY
You track the mitigation plans of the risk team of a pharmaceutical company. You classify each plan by its evidence and prepare requests and alerts for the analyst to approve; you do not mark plans as completed.

CONTEXT
acceptance_criteria.md holds the acceptance criteria by action type and the rescheduling rule: at most 2, each with the director's approval and a recorded justification.

INPUT
plans.csv with id, source, action_type, action, owner, manager, original_deadline, current_deadline, reschedulings, declared_status, rescheduling_justification. Evidence files with the plan id at the start of the name. emails.md with the e-mails with the id in the subject. previous_cycle.csv with id and classification.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. List, per plan, the files and what each one proves.
2. Compare with the acceptance criterion of the action type: item met and item missing.
3. Classify as completed with evidence, completed without evidence, in progress on time, overdue up to 60 days, overdue over 60 days, rescheduled outside the rule.
4. Days of delay are calendar days up to today, from the current deadline; from the original deadline when the rescheduling has no recorded justification or the plan has a regulatory source.
5. Draft the evidence request for those completed without evidence, citing the missing item.
6. Compare with previous_cycle.csv and list the plans that changed band.

RULES AND LIMITS
A statement in an e-mail is not evidence. A health inspection document enters only by its identifier, with no batch or content. Do not propose a new deadline. A plan with a regulatory source is never reschedulable. More than 2 reschedulings: rescheduled outside the rule.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Distribution line by status. Then one block per plan outside \"in progress on time\": id | source | action | owner | declared status | evidence found | criterion met or not | days of delay | classification | proposed message and who approves. Close with the plans that changed band.

ESCALATION
Delay up to 60 days: request to the owner, approved by the analyst. Delay over 60 days or third rescheduling: message to the owner's manager, approved by the risk manager, and agenda item for the monthly meeting. A plan with a regulatory source and any delay: also an immediate alert to the agency relations lead and the quality director.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"Pharma Mitigation Plans Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder Pharma Mitigation Plans Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file PHARMAMITIGATE_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

# Acceptance criteria and rescheduling rule (example)

## Acceptance criteria by action type
| action_type | Item 1 | Item 2 |
|---|---|---|
| procedure | document in a new version, approved and dated | training record of the people involved |
| training | signed attendance list | effectiveness assessment applied |
| system_control | screenshot or export of the configuration | test evidence (one approved test transaction) |
| physical_change | execution report | approved qualification |
Completed with evidence requires both items.

## Rescheduling
At most 2 per plan, each with the director's approval and a justification recorded in rescheduling_justification. Source health_inspection is regulatory: never reschedulable, the delay counts from the original deadline.

## Classification order
1. declared_status completed: with evidence or without evidence, by the 2 items.
2. More than 2 reschedulings: rescheduled outside the rule.
3. Others: on time, overdue up to 60 days or overdue over 60 days, by the days of delay.

## Rules with no leeway
- A rescheduling with no recorded justification does not count: the delay counts from the original deadline. E.g.: PM-070 has current deadline 2026-12-10, but with no justification it counts from 2026-10-15: 32 days, overdue up to 60.
- A regulatory source always counts from the original deadline, even with an approved rescheduling, and every band applies. E.g.: PM-072, 16 days since 2026-10-31: request to the owner and alert to the agency relations lead and the quality director.
- An e-mail is not evidence. E.g.: the "deployed" of PM-064 and the "should be out next week" of PM-075 change nothing.
- A health inspection document only by its identifier, in any part of the output. E.g.: cite RI-2026-05, with no batch or excerpt.
- Math. E.g.: PM-075, 67 days since 2026-09-10, over 60; PM-067, 3 reschedulings, outside the rule.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not mark a plan as completed: it classifies the evidence against the criterion and the analyst records it. No message about a delay goes out without human approval, because chasing a deadline on behalf of the risk team carries hierarchical weight. Evidence from health inspections contains batch data under regulatory confidentiality and appears in the output only by the document identifier. A plan with a regulatory origin (health surveillance inspection) is not rescheduled through the internal flow: any delay goes to whoever owns the relationship with the agency.

Common mistakes

  • Accepting an "implemented" email as evidence; auditors and inspectors ask for the artifact, not the declaration.
  • Rescheduling the deadline and resetting the delay count before the approval authority signs off.
  • Treating a health inspection plan as an internal plan with a negotiable deadline; the deadline was committed to the agency.
  • Closing the plan with the procedure published but without training the people who carry it out; the next audit finds the new SOP and the old practice.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Plans completed with evidence that meets the criterionfrom 42 of the 73 declared to 95% or more of those completed with accepted evidenceestimate based on the described routine
Reschedulings with no approved justificationfrom 18 plans to zero in 2 monthly cyclesprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine); estimate based on the described routine
Share of the monthly meeting spent gathering statusfrom about 50% to less than 15%estimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Follow-up of 2026-09-15, 73 plans.

Distribution: completed with evidence 24 | completed without evidence 9 | in progress on time 17 | overdue up to 60 days 11 | overdue more than 60 days 7 | rescheduled outside the rule 5.

PM-041 | origin: health inspection 2026-03, item 7 | action: revise the cleaning SOP for the weighing room | owner: production coordination | declared status: completed on 2026-08-20 | evidence found: POP-LP-014 version 6 in the folder, approved on 2026-08-18, and a training record for 14 operators | acceptance criterion: met | classification: COMPLETED WITH EVIDENCE.

PM-052 | origin: risk committee R-09 | action: implement dual approval for bank detail changes in the ERP | owner: corporate IT | declared status: completed | evidence found: email of 2026-07-30 saying "implemented"; no configuration screenshot or test | acceptance criterion: not met | classification: COMPLETED WITHOUT EVIDENCE | proposed message to the owner: request for a screenshot of the rule and 1 approved test change (awaiting the analyst's approval).

PM-033 | origin: quality audit 2025-11 | action: qualify an alternative excipient supplier | original deadline 2026-02-28, current deadline 2026-10-31, 3 reschedulings, the last with no recorded justification | classification: RESCHEDULED OUTSIDE THE RULE (the limit is 2 with the director's approval) | action: mandatory item on the meeting agenda.

Plans that passed 60 days overdue this fortnight: 2 (PM-019, PM-027); message to the manager proposed, awaiting approval.
